summary: 看似同时做几件事，大脑往往要在任务间反复切换。心理学实验量出了切换的时间代价，文章进一步讨论工作压力和专注力，由此解释逐项完成任务的好处。
logic: 从办公室里的多任务切入

paragraphs.brief: 办公室里接连发生的任务切换
sentences: You arrive at the office, review your to-do list and start to feel a headache coming on.
你来到办公室，检查你的待办事宜清单并开始感到头痛了。
You resolve to tackle the items as quickly as possible.
你决定尽快把清单上的事情一项项处理掉。
While you return calls, you sort e-mail and other letters.
当你回电话时，你整理电子邮件和其他信件。
You begin keying in slides for tomorrow’s presentation.
你开始在电脑上为明天的演示制作幻灯片。
Then your manager comes in wanting an immediate update on sales figures.
之后你的经理想马上得到销售数据的最新信息
You have just opened the spreadsheet when a very important customer calls.
电子表格刚打开，一位重要客户又打来了电话。
With the receiver held between your shoulder and your ear, you continue adding up the sales totals until, 15 minutes later, you finally manage, politely, to get rid of the client.
你用肩膀和耳朵夹住听筒，继续合计销售额，十五分钟后才终于设法礼貌地结束通话。
You’ve been multitasking again.
你又开始多任务了。
paragraphs.gist: 办公室里回电话、整理邮件和准备简报还没做完，经理与客户又先后来找，作者用这一连串打断呈现日常多任务工作的样子。

paragraphs.brief: 同时赶工可能耗时又出错
sentences: You may believe that anyone who wants to get ahead today should master the art of multitasking.
你可能会相信任何今天想领先的人都应该掌握多任务艺术
However, a recent study by the Families and Work Institute in New York City has found that 45 per cent of US workers believe that they are asked or expected to work on too many tasks at once.
然而，纽约市家庭和工作研究所最近的一项研究发现，45%的美国工人认为他们被要求或预期同时从事过多的工作。
Managers may be surprised to learn that they are actually wasting their workers’ time.
管理者可能惊讶地得知他们实际上在浪费工人的时间。
As it turns out, the human brain cannot really master the computer’s art of crunching data in the background while moving between process windows.
人的大脑无法像电脑那样，在各个程序窗口之间切换时仍在后台运算数据。
Instead, a growing number of studies show that trying to juggle jobs rather than completing them sequentially can take longer and leave workers with a reduced ability to perform each task.
越来越多的研究显示，相比逐项完成，几份工作来回穿插可能更费时，而且每一件都做得更差。
In addition, the stress associated with multitasking may contribute to short-term memory difficulties.
此外，与多任务有关的压力可能会造成短期记忆困难。

The combination results in inefficiency, careless thinking and mistakes – not to mention the possible dangers of divided attention for drivers, air-traffic controllers and others who handle machinery.
这种结合导致效率低下、思维不谨慎和错误，更不用说对司机、空中交通控制员和其他操作机器的人的注意力分散可能造成的危险。
paragraphs.gist: 近半数受访美国员工觉得同时要做的事太多，研究也发现任务来回切换既拖慢进度、影响记忆，还可能带来差错与危险。

paragraphs.brief: 斯特鲁普实验证明任务干扰
sentences: How can a time-management strategy that has become part of the common wisdom actually be so wrong?
一套被视作常识的时间管理策略，怎么会错到这个地步？
Exploring that question requires a closer look at an area of consciousness research that examines how the brain focuses attention.
要探讨这个问题，就必须更仔细地研究一个研究大脑如何集中注意力的意识研究领域。

One of the modern foundations of current knowledge of multitasking was laid in 1935, when the American psychologist John Ridley Stroop reported that processing information from one task could cause interference with another.
1935年，美国心理学家约翰·里德利·斯特鲁普发现，处理一项任务的信息可能干扰另一项任务，为现代多任务研究奠定了基础。

Stroop noticed that when study participants were asked to name the colour of a word – such as ‘green’ – printed in a different colour – red, for example – they experienced difficulty saying the name of the colour.
斯特鲁普发现，一个词若用与字义不同的颜色印出，例如用红色印「绿」，受试者就很难说出墨水的颜色。

This phenomenon is thought to occur when two tasks get tangled: the brain must suppress one that has been learned so well that it has become automatic (reading) to attend to a second task that requires concentration (naming the colour).
可能的解释是两项任务互相干扰：大脑要抑制熟练到近乎自动的阅读反应，才能集中精力完成第二项任务，即说出颜色。
paragraphs.gist: 斯特鲁普让受试者说出印刷颜色而忽略字义，发现自动化的阅读会干扰报出颜色，说明一项任务的信息处理能妨碍另一项。

paragraphs.brief: 三秒时间窗解释注意力限制
sentences: During the past couple of decades, psychologists have probed more deeply into the nature and limitations of multitasking.
在过去的几十年里，心理学家们更深入地探讨了多重任务的性质和局限性。

Psychologist and brain-researcher Ernst Pöppel, of the Ludwig-Maximilian University in Munich, believes that it is impossible to carry out two or three different tasks simultaneously with the same degree of concentration.
慕尼黑大学心理学家兼脑科学家恩斯特·珀佩尔认为，人不可能同时做两三件不同的事，还对每件都保持同样程度的专注。
He says that seemingly simultaneous awareness and processing of information actually take place in ‘three-second windows’.
他说，似乎同时对信息的认识和处理实际上发生在 " 三秒钟的窗口 "。
paragraphs.gist: 心理学家珀佩尔认为，人无法同等专注于几件事，看似同步发生的觉察与处理，实际上分布在一个个三秒的时间窗内。

paragraphs.brief: 刺激如何轮流进入注意中心
sentences: In these three-second segments, the brain takes in, as a block, all the data about the environment streaming in from the sensory systems; subsequent events are processed in the next window.
在每个三秒时段内，大脑把感官送来的环境信息作为整体接收，随后的事件则在下一个时间窗处理。
So a person can concentrate on a conversation for three seconds, then for three seconds on a crying child, and three seconds on a computer screen.
人可以用三秒专心听对话，接着用三秒注意哭泣的孩子，再用三秒看电脑屏幕。
While one subject at a time occupies the foreground of consciousness, the others stay in the background until they, in turn, are given access to the central processor.
每次只有一个对象占据意识的前台，其他对象留在背景，等到轮流进入中央处理环节。
paragraphs.gist: 按三秒时间窗的解释，谈话、孩子的哭声和屏幕会轮流进入注意中心，其他刺激暂留背景，等待大脑转向它们。

paragraphs.brief: 切换规则增加任务耗时
sentences: Another experiment by psychologist David E. Meyer, of the University of Michigan, quantified just how much time we can lose when we shuttle between tasks.
密歇根大学心理学家大卫·迈耶的另一项实验量化了在任务之间穿梭时我们能损失多少时间
The researchers asked test participants to write a report and check their e-mail at the same time.
研究人员要求测试参与者同时撰写报告和检查他们的电子邮件。
Those individuals who constantly jumped back and forth between the two tasks took about one and a half times as long to finish as those who completed one job before turning to the other.
不停在报告和邮件间切换的人，完成两件事所需的时间约为先做完一件再做另一件者的1.5倍。
Each switchover from one task to another meant re-thinking and thus involved additional neural resources.
每次改变任务都意味着要重新理清思路，因此需要额外的神经资源。
In effect, the brain needs time to shut off the rules for one task and to turn on the rules for another.
事实上，大脑需要时间来关闭一项任务的规则，并打开另一项任务的规则。
‘Multitasking saves time only when it is a matter of relaxed, routine tasks,’ Meyer says.
迈耶说：「只有处理轻松、例行的事务时，多任务才省时。」
It also takes the brain longer to adapt when switching rapidly back to an interrupted task rather than waiting longer before switching back.
与隔久一点再切回相比，匆忙回到刚被打断的任务，大脑需要更长的适应时间。
paragraphs.gist: 迈耶发现，报告和邮件交替做约需依次完成时的一点五倍时间，因为切换要重新启动任务规则，匆忙切回也会增加适应时间。

paragraphs.brief: 多任务压力影响前额叶和记忆
sentences: By its nature multitasking is stressful, and the area in the brain most involved with multitasking is also most affected by the resulting stress.
多任务本身就会造成压力，而参与多任务最深的脑区也最容易受这种压力影响。
Located behind the forehead, the prefrontal cortex – which neuroscientists call the ‘executive’ part of the brain – helps us to assess tasks, prioritise them and assign mental resources.
前额叶皮层位于额头后方，神经科学家称它是大脑的「执行」部分，帮助我们评估任务、安排轻重缓急并分配认知资源。
It also ‘marks’ the spot at which a task has been interrupted, so that we can return to it later.
它还会「标记」任务中断的位置，以便我们稍后能够接着做。

This stress can also affect brain cells in another region, the hippocampus, which is important for forming new memories; damage in that area also makes it difficult for a person to acquire new skills.
压力还可能影响海马体内的脑细胞；海马体对形成新记忆很重要，受损后也会使人难以掌握新技能。
paragraphs.gist: 多任务带来的压力恰会影响负责安排优先顺序、记住中断位置的前额叶，也可能波及形成新记忆、帮助学习技能的海马体。

paragraphs.brief: 先完成简报再看邮件的理由
sentences: Psychiatrists Edward Hallowell and John Ratey, of Harvard University, say that multitasking can bring about a brain condition that causes sufferers to constantly seek new information while having difficulties concentrating on its content.
哈佛大学精神科医生爱德华·哈洛韦尔和约翰·雷蒂认为，多任务可能使人不断寻找新信息，却很难专注于信息内容。
All in all, it may be wise to let the e-mail wait while you work on your presentation.
总之，做简报时不妨先让邮件等一等。
You will save time and perform each task better.
你会节省时间，更好地执行每项任务。
paragraphs.gist: 两位精神科医生指出，多任务可能使人不断寻求新信息却无法专注于内容，因此作者建议先做完简报再查看邮件。

items.en: Less attention will be paid to each task when more than one task is attempted at the same time.
items.zh: 同时做几件事时，分给每项任务的注意力都会减少。

items.en: Repeated changes of task mean that the brain will take a while to adjust.
items.zh: 任务反复改变意味着大脑需要一段时间才能适应。

items.en: Using the skills required for one task may make performing another one more difficult.
items.zh: 使用一项任务所需的技能可能会使另一项任务更难完成。

items.en: When multitasking, the brain can only focus on single tasks for very short periods.
items.zh: 同时处理多项任务时，大脑每次只能短暂地专注于其中一项。

items.en: Multitasking can lead to a medical problem.
items.zh: 同时处理多项任务可能引发健康问题。

items.zh: 本文的主要目的是什么？

质疑人们普遍持有的关于同时处理多项任务的看法。

points: 回到对应内容“前额叶皮层位于额头后方，神经科学家称它是大脑的「执行」部分，帮助我们评估任务、安排轻重缓急并分配认知资源”，再按题干要求写出答案。
题干问“多重任务可能导致医疗问题”。定位句写到“哈佛大学的精神病学家爱德华·哈洛韦尔和约翰·拉斯蒂说，多重任务可以带来一种大脑状况，使患者在关注新信息的内容时遇到困难，从而导致他们不断寻找新信息”。
clauses: “that anyone who wants to get ahead today should master the art of multitasking”补足 believe 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 believe 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
How can a time-management strategy … actually be so wrong?
“that has become part of the common wisdom”修饰前面的 strategy。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 that 时，回看 strategy，再把修饰信息接回主句。
lead: Doing more than one thing at once – is it always a good idea?
